label: Metal vs CUDA on the matched all-minilm-l6-v2 embed contract: what is comparable, and what is refused
question: On the one contract candle, llama.cpp and vLLM can all be held to, what may be compared across an M3 Ultra and a rented A40?

matched_contract.note: candle and vLLM load the SAME safetensors bytes; llama.cpp loads the governed F16 GGUF of the same model

quality_verdict.consequence: all three engines are the same product on this contract; a placement decision between them cannot be a quality decision

latency_engine_side.cuda_boundary: vllm:request_inference_time_seconds, engine-published, excludes the client link
latency_engine_side.metal_boundary: client wall over loopback (llama.cpp) and in-process (candle); both from the BOUND parity receipt
latency_engine_side.caveat: the boundaries are not identical: vLLM's figure covers scheduling plus forward pass, llama.cpp's is client wall on loopback, candle's has no socket at all. They are the same order of magnitude and the ranking is stable, which is as strong a statement as these instruments support. It is not a controlled cross-hardware latency benchmark.

throughput_verdict.why: the A40 reported 1.23 ms/request of queueing against 43.6 ms of inference, so it was never the bottleneck. 206 ms of every 250 ms request was not inference: urllib opens a fresh TCP+TLS connection per request and the link is ~100 ms. The client-observed 223 units/s is a property of this laptop and the network. No throughput ceiling for the A40 was established and none is claimed.
throughput_verdict.what_would_establish_one: a load generator running ON the pod, or a keep-alive client saturating the engine until queue time exceeds inference time

cost_verdict.why: cost may not be compared across hardware classes; the difference between an M3 Ultra and a rented A40 is the machine, not the placement

placement_thesis.why: the three-arm mixed-traffic thesis needs Merc selecting per contract, and ordinary admission freezes exactly one advertised cell per (job type, model). Arm C cannot exist on this tree. Renting more GPUs does not change that; it is a routing-authority question, not a capacity one.

does_not_prove: a cost winner between Metal and CUDA
a throughput ceiling for the A40, or for any hardware class
that vllm-cuda-minilm-embed may be routed or advertised; it stays DRAFT
a fleet claim, or behaviour at another batch size, model or precision
that production routing changed in any way

exact_config.value: A40 secure $0.44/hr cap $1.00; vLLM 0.23.0 --runner pooling --max-model-len 256 --max-num-seqs 64; concurrency 1,4,16,64 rounds 6; Metal llama-server -np 64 --pooling mean

raw_samples.value: cuda sweep 4080 requests; metal sweep 4 levels; see embed-throughput-*-latest.json
